parsed.doc_summary: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act just-cause eviction), as amended by AB 1529, operative 2024-04-01, effective 2026-01-01 amendment, repealed 2030-01-01. Requires just cause after 12 months of occupancy, relocation assistance of one month's rent for no-fault terminations, with exemptions and deference to local ordinances.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit for 12 months, the owner can end the tenancy only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault reasons the owner must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and the notice must say so.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.effective_date_note: Section operative April 1, 2024 per subd. (m); the version as amended by AB 1529 took effect 2026-01-01. Original TPA effective 2020-01-01 (not stated in this document).
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; owner shares bathroom/kitchen; owner-occupied single-family (up to two units/bedrooms rented) and owner-occupied duplex; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property owned by non-REIT/corporation/LLC-with-corporate-member with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenant must have occupied 12 months (or 24 months if additional adult tenants added).
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019, or a later more protective local ordinance, applies; property cannot be subject to both.
rules.penalty: Noncompliant notice is void; owner liable for actual damages, attorney's fees, up to three times actual damages if willful; AG, city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.conflict_note: Yields to local just-cause ordinances (e.g., LA, SF, Berkeley) that are earlier or more protective.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes/condos alienable separately owned by non-corporate owner with notice
dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transient hotels
